name: Sichuan Eggplant
assumptions: Yield estimated at 4 servings based on 1.5 lb eggplant as primary ingredient, typical for 4 side or 2-3 main portions in Chinese stir-fry recipes; conservative classification used.
Peanut oil classifies as peanuts allergen present.
Soy sauce and chili bean paste (containing soybeans) classify as soy allergen present.
Wheat allergen null due to possible wheat in soy sauce or chili bean paste but not explicitly confirmed in all variants.
Fish allergen null due to possible fish sauce in some chicken stocks or pastes but not listed.
Minutes estimated from mise en place (10 min) + sauté and simmer steps (20 min total active cooking).
Chicken stock makes vegetarian/vegan false per dietary screening; no gluten-free confirmation as soy sauce and pastes often contain wheat.
instructions:
This recipe calls for asian eggplants, or Japanese eggplants. They are long and thin compared to a European or globe eggplant, and much more tender and delicate. If you can't find them you can substitute globe eggplant, but the dish is really best with the asian eggplant.

*A lot of grocery stores have Asian ingredient aisles now. You should be able to find chili-bean paste, a mixture of preserved chilies mixed with mashed soybeans, there or at any Asian market. (Do not confuse with black bean paste or chili-garlic paste.)

**Sichuan peppercorns are available at some stores and online for quite cheap. They aren't spicy like other peppers but rather have a citrusy flavor and induce a tingly, numbing sensation like a carbonated drink.

Prep eggplant, chili sauce, cornstarch slurry, vinegar and scallions:
Begin your mise en place. Quarter the eggplant lengthwise and chop into large batons and set aside.

In a small bowl, mix together the chicken stock, sugar, and soy sauce and set it aside.

In a second bowl, mix together the chili bean paste, garlic, ginger, and sichuan peppercorns and set it aside.

In a third bowl, mix together the cornstarch with a tablespoon of water and set it aside.

Lastly, in a fourth bowl, mix together the scallions and vinegar and set it aside.

Sauté eggplant:
Place the oil in a wok or large sauté pan over medium-high heat until the oil is almost smoking. Add the eggplant and sauté, allowing it to sit for a few seconds each time you move it to allow it to brown and blister. If the eggplant absorbs all the oil and some pieces don't get any then add a little more oil.

Add the chili bean paste, garlic, ginger, and sichuan peppercorns and sauté:
until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add the chicken stock mixture:
turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 90 seconds.

Add the cornstarch mixture:
and stir together until the sauce thickens a bit.

Add the scallions and vinegar:
and cook for 15 seconds to diffuse their harsh flavors a bit.

Garnish with cilantro and serve.

ingredients.name: Egg Plants
ingredients.assumptions: 1.5 lb = 680g raw Asian/Japanese eggplant (edible portion); typical nutrition for raw eggplant adjusted for long thin variety.

ingredients.name: Peanut Oil
ingredients.assumptions: 2 tbsp peanut oil = 28g; standard cooking oil density and full fat content.

ingredients.name: Chicken Stock
ingredients.assumptions: 1/4 cup chicken stock ≈ 60g; typical low-sodium broth values, mostly water with minimal macros.

ingredients.name: Soy Sauce
ingredients.assumptions: 1/2 tsp soy sauce ≈ 3g; standard fermented soy sauce nutrition.

ingredients.name: Chilli Bean Paste
ingredients.assumptions: 1.5 tbsp chili bean paste (doubanjiang) ≈ 24g; typical values for fermented chili-soybean paste, estimated from similar condiments.

ingredients.name: Sichuan Pepper
ingredients.assumptions: 2 tsp ground Sichuan peppercorns ≈ 4g; low-calorie spice with typical pepper nutrition.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.assumptions: 2 tsp minced fresh ginger ≈ 4g; standard raw ginger root values.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.assumptions: 5 cloves garlic ≈ 15g; typical raw garlic nutrition.

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tsp cornstarch ≈ 3g; nearly pure carbohydrate starch.

ingredients.name: Apple Cider Vinegar
ingredients.assumptions: 2 tsp apple cider vinegar ≈ 10g; typical vinegar nutrition, mostly water with trace carbs.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.assumptions: 4 chopped scallions ≈ 60g (about 4 medium); raw green onion values.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.assumptions: Cilantro garnish estimated at 10g (small handful); typical raw cilantro leaves nutrition for a plated garnish.
